source.text: מַשָּׂ֖א צֹ֑ר הֵילִ֣ילוּ׀אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־שֻׁדַּ֤ד מִבַּ֨יִת֙ מִבּ֔וֹא מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כִּתִּ֖ים נִגְלָה־לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] oracle [of] Tyre. Wail, ships of Tarshish, for it has been devastated, from house, from coming in; from [the] land of Kittim it has been revealed to them.

en.L: The oracle of Tyre. \q Wail, ships of Tarshish, for it is devastated, without house, without entering; \q from the land of Kittim it has been revealed to them.
en.B: The oracle concerning Tyre. \q Wail, ships of Tarshish! Tyre lies in ruins, with no house left standing and no port to come home to. \q From the land of Kittim the news has reached them.
en.R: This is a message about Tyre. \q Cry out in grief, you sailors on the great trading ships! Tyre has been destroyed. No houses are left, and there is no harbor where your ships can come home. \q You heard the news on the way home, in Cyprus.

es.L: Oráculo de Tiro. \q {{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, naves de Tarsis, porque está devastada, sin casa, sin entrada; \q desde la tierra de Quitim les ha sido revelado.
es.B: Oráculo sobre Tiro. \q ¡{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, naves de Tarsis! Tiro está en ruinas, sin una casa en pie ni un puerto adonde volver. \q Desde la tierra de Quitim les ha llegado la noticia.
es.R: Este es un mensaje sobre Tiro. \q ¡{{plural_you:Lloren de dolor, ustedes|Llorad de dolor, vosotros}}, marineros de los grandes barcos mercantes! Tiro ha sido destruida. No quedan casas, y no hay puerto donde {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} barcos puedan volver. \q {{plural_you:Se enteraron|Os enterasteis}} de la noticia de regreso a casa, en Chipre.

fr.L: Oracle [concernant] Tyr. \q Lamentez-vous, navires de Tarsis, car elle est dévastée, plus de maison, plus d’entrée ; \q depuis le pays des Kittim, cela leur a été révélé.
fr.B: Oracle sur Tyr. \q Lamentez-vous, navires de Tarsis ! Tyr est en ruine, il n’y reste plus une maison, plus un port où rentrer. \q C’est au pays des Kittim que la nouvelle les a rejoints.
fr.R: Message au sujet de Tyr. \q Criez de douleur, vous, les marins des grands navires de commerce ! Tyr a été détruite. Il ne reste plus de maisons, et il n’y a plus de port où vos navires puissent rentrer. \q Vous avez appris la nouvelle sur le chemin du retour, à Chypre.

sw.L: Unabii [juu ya] Tiro. \q Ombolezeni, enyi merikebu za Tarshishi, kwa maana umeharibiwa, hakuna nyumba, hakuna kuingia; \q kutoka nchi ya Kitimu imefunuliwa kwao.
sw.B: Unabii kuhusu Tiro. \q Ombolezeni, enyi merikebu za Tarshishi! Tiro umeharibiwa, hakuna nyumba iliyobaki wala bandari ya kurudia. \q Habari zimewafikia kutoka nchi ya Kitimu.
sw.R: Ujumbe kuhusu Tiro. \q Lieni kwa huzuni, enyi mabaharia wa meli kubwa za biashara! Tiro umeharibiwa. Hakuna nyumba zilizobaki, wala hakuna bandari ambamo meli zenu zinaweza kurudi. \q Mlisikia habari hizo mlipokuwa njiani kurudi nyumbani, huko Kipro.

decisions.choice: oracle: a weighty message from God
decisions.reason: The word heads the oracles against the nations (see the note at 13:1). This one concerns Tyre, the great Phoenician port on an island off the coast, and its sister city Sidon (verses 2, 4, 12).

decisions.choice: ships of Tarshish: large seagoing trading ships
decisions.reason: Tarshish was a distant port far to the west (Jonah 1:3); its name was given to the large ships that made such long voyages (2:16; 1 Kings 10:22). The poem opens and closes with these ships (verse 14).

decisions.choice: without house, without entering: Tyre is left with no home and no harbor; the sailors learn it at Kittim
alternatives: destroyed, so that no one can enter from home
decisions.reason: The two short phrases say Tyre is destroyed so that there is no house and no way in. Kittim is Cyprus (its city Kition), the last stop for ships sailing home to Tyre from the west.

decisions.choice: message
decisions.reason: Readable says "message" for "oracle", as at 13:1.

decisions.choice: great trading ships
decisions.reason: Readable says what ships of Tarshish were: large ships built for long trading voyages (2:16). Readable speaks to the sailors on them.

decisions.choice: Tyre / no port to come home to; Cyprus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Tyre as the city destroyed and say what "without entering" means for ships. Readable says "Cyprus" for Kittim.

decisions.choice: Giman, naves de Tarsis (L, B); Lloren de dolor ... grandes barcos mercantes (R)
decisions.reason: The block's forms for helilu and the ships of Tarshish, as the terms note and 1 Kings 10:22; the plural command is a plural_you span.

decisions.choice: Quitim (L, B); Chipre (R)
decisions.reason: Kittim keeps its published name (Genesis 10:4) at L and B; Readable names Cyprus, as the English R.

decisions.choice: "merikebu za Tarshishi" (L, B); "meli kubwa za biashara" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note keeps "merikebu za Tarshishi" of Psalm 48:8 at Literal and Balanced; Readable explains them as the English does. Readable "Kipro" for Kittim follows Acts 11:19.

decisions.choice: "Ombolezeni" (L, B); "Lieni kwa huzuni" (R)
decisions.reason: The call to wail (helilu) is "ombolezeni", the word for lament over the dead, at Literal and Balanced throughout this block; Readable says "cry out in grief" plainly.

decisions.choice: "Lamentez-vous" (L, B), "Criez de douleur" (R) for helilu, for Isaiah 21-40
decisions.reason: "Hurlez" sounds like animal howling in modern French; "se lamenter" is the loud grief of mourners, and Readable says it plainly, as the English "Cry out in grief".

decisions.choice: "navires de Tarsis" (L, B), "grands navires de commerce" (R); "les Kittim" (L, B), "Chypre" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note and 1 Kings 10:22.

source.text: דֹּ֖מּוּ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי אִ֑י סֹחֵ֥ר צִיד֛וֹן עֹבֵ֥ר יָ֖ם מִלְאֽוּךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Be silent, inhabitants of [the] coastland, merchant of Sidon, passing over [the] sea, they have filled you.

en.L: Be silent, inhabitants of the coastland! \q The merchants of Sidon, crossing [the] sea, filled you.
en.B: Be still, you people of the coast, \q whom Sidon's traders filled with wealth as they sailed the sea.
en.R: Be quiet, you people who live on the coast. \q Traders from Sidon sailed across the sea and made you rich.

es.L: ¡{{plural_you:Callen|Callad}}, habitantes de la costa! \q Los mercaderes de Sidón, que cruzaban [el] mar, te llenaron.
es.B: {{plural_you:Guarden|Guardad}} silencio, gente de la costa, \q a quienes los comerciantes de Sidón llenaron de riquezas al surcar el mar.
es.R: {{plural_you:Quédense callados, ustedes que viven|Quedaos callados, vosotros que vivís}} en la costa. \q Los comerciantes de Sidón cruzaban el mar y {{plural_you:los|os}} hicieron ricos.

fr.L: Taisez-vous, habitants de la côte ! \q Les marchands de Sidon, traversant la mer, t’ont remplie.
fr.B: Restez muets, gens de la côte, \q que les marchands de Sidon ont remplis de richesses en parcourant la mer.
fr.R: Taisez-vous, vous qui habitez sur la côte. \q Les marchands de Sidon traversaient la mer et vous ont rendus riches.

sw.L: Nyamazeni, enyi wakaaji wa pwani! \q Wafanyabiashara wa Sidoni, wakivuka bahari, walikujaza.
sw.B: Tulieni, enyi watu wa pwani, \q ambao wafanyabiashara wa Sidoni waliwajaza mali walipokuwa wakisafiri baharini.
sw.R: Kaeni kimya, enyi watu mnaoishi pwani. \q Wafanyabiashara kutoka Sidoni walivuka bahari wakawatajirisha.

decisions.choice: be silent: be stunned into silence, as mourners are
decisions.reason: The verb means to be still or silent; here it is the silence of shock and grief (compare Lamentations 2:10).

decisions.choice: the merchant of Sidon: the merchants as a group, who filled the coast with goods and wealth
decisions.reason: The word is singular but the verb "they filled" is plural, so the merchant stands for all of Sidon's traders. The coastland is the Phoenician coast of Tyre and Sidon.

decisions.choice: crossing the sea, they filled you: the traditional Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads "they crossed the sea, your messengers", joining the words to the start of verse 3. The traditional text gives good sense and is followed here; reviewers should check the scroll's wording.

decisions.choice: filled with wealth / made you rich
decisions.reason: "Filled you" means filled with goods and riches; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וּבְמַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ זֶ֣רַע שִׁחֹ֔ר קְצִ֥יר יְא֖וֹר תְּבֽוּאָתָ֑הּ וַתְּהִ֖י סְחַ֥ר גּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And on many waters [was] [the] seed of Shihor, [the] harvest of [the] Nile [was] her revenue; and she became [the] market of nations.

en.L: And on many waters [came] the grain of Shihor; \q the harvest of the Nile [was] her revenue, \q and she became the market of nations.
en.B: The grain of Shihor crossed the mighty waters; \q what the Nile harvested brought her income, \q and she grew into a market for the nations.
en.R: Ships carried grain from Egypt across the sea. \q The crops that grew beside the Nile River made Tyre rich. \q She became the place where the nations came to buy and sell.

es.L: Y sobre muchas aguas [venía] el grano de Sihor; \q la cosecha del Nilo [era] su ganancia, \q y llegó a ser el mercado de las naciones.
es.B: El grano de Sihor cruzaba las grandes aguas; \q lo que cosechaba el Nilo le daba sus ganancias, \q y llegó a ser un mercado para las naciones.
es.R: Los barcos traían grano de Egipto a través del mar. \q Las cosechas que crecían junto al río Nilo hicieron rica a Tiro. \q Llegó a ser el lugar adonde las naciones iban a comprar y vender.

fr.L: Et sur les grandes eaux [venait] le grain de Shihor ; \q la moisson du Nil [était] son revenu, \q et elle est devenue le marché des nations.
fr.B: Le grain de Shihor traversait les grandes eaux ; \q les récoltes du Nil faisaient son revenu, \q et elle est devenue le marché des nations.
fr.R: Des navires transportaient le blé d’Égypte à travers la mer. \q Les récoltes qui poussaient au bord du Nil ont enrichi Tyr. \q Elle est devenue l’endroit où les nations venaient acheter et vendre.

sw.L: Na juu ya maji mengi [ilikuja] nafaka ya Shihori; \q mavuno ya Naili [yalikuwa] mapato yake, \q naye akawa soko la mataifa.
sw.B: Nafaka ya Shihori ilivuka maji makuu; \q mavuno ya Naili yalimletea mapato, \q naye akawa soko la mataifa.
sw.R: Meli zilibeba nafaka kutoka Misri kuvuka bahari. \q Mazao yaliyoota kando ya mto Naili yaliutajirisha Tiro. \q Tiro ukawa mahali ambapo mataifa yalikuja kununua na kuuza.

decisions.choice: Shihor and the Nile: the waters of Egypt and its grain
decisions.reason: Shihor is a water at the edge of Egypt, probably a branch of the Nile (Joshua 13:3; Jeremiah 2:18). Egypt's grain was carried by Phoenician ships, and Tyre grew rich on the trade.

decisions.choice: her: Tyre, the city addressed in the poem
decisions.reason: The feminine pronoun refers to the city. Cities are spoken of as women throughout the chapter (verses 7, 12, 15-17).

decisions.choice: Ships carried grain from Egypt / made Tyre rich
decisions.reason: Readable says that the grain came by ship from Egypt and names Tyre for "her".

decisions.choice: "naye akawa"
decisions.reason: The poem pictures Tyre as a woman, so Literal and Balanced speak of her with the personal pronoun "yeye"; Readable, which names the city, uses the agreement of "mji".

source.text: בּ֣וֹשִׁי צִיד֔וֹן כִּֽי־אָמַ֣ר יָ֔ם מָע֥וֹז הַיָּ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹֽא־חַ֣לְתִּי וְלֹֽא־יָלַ֗דְתִּי וְלֹ֥א גִדַּ֛לְתִּי בַּחוּרִ֖ים רוֹמַ֥מְתִּי בְתוּלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Be ashamed, Sidon, for has said [the] sea, [the] stronghold of the sea, saying, not I have been in labor and not I have given birth, and not I have brought up young men, I have raised young women.

en.L: Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, \q the stronghold of the sea, saying, \q "I have not been in labor and I have not given birth, and I have not brought up young men, [nor] raised young women."
en.B: Hang your head in shame, Sidon, \q because the sea, the sea's stronghold, cries out: \q "I have known no labor pains and borne no children; I have raised no young men and brought up no young women."
en.R: Sidon, be ashamed! \q The sea has spoken, the strong fortress out in the sea. It says, \q "I am like a woman who has no children. I never went through labor or gave birth. I never raised boys to be young men or girls to be young women."

es.L: Avergüénzate, Sidón, porque ha hablado el mar, \q la fortaleza del mar, diciendo: \q «No he estado de parto ni he dado a luz, ni he criado jóvenes, [ni] he educado doncellas».
es.B: Baja la cabeza avergonzada, Sidón, \q porque el mar, la fortaleza del mar, exclama: \q «No he conocido dolores de parto ni he tenido hijos; no he criado muchachos ni he educado muchachas».
es.R: ¡Sidón, avergüénzate! \q El mar ha hablado, la fuerte fortaleza en medio del mar. Dice: \q «Soy como una mujer que no tiene hijos. Nunca estuve de parto ni di a luz. Nunca crie niños hasta hacerlos hombres, ni niñas hasta hacerlas mujeres».

fr.L: Sois honteuse, Sidon, car la mer a parlé, \q la forteresse de la mer, disant : \q « Je n’ai pas été en travail et je n’ai pas enfanté, et je n’ai pas élevé de jeunes gens, [ni] fait grandir de jeunes filles. »
fr.B: Baisse la tête de honte, Sidon, \q car la mer, la forteresse de la mer, s’écrie : \q « Je n’ai pas connu les douleurs, je n’ai pas mis d’enfants au monde ; je n’ai pas élevé de jeunes gens, ni fait grandir de jeunes filles. »
fr.R: Sidon, sois couverte de honte ! \q La mer a parlé, la forteresse solide au milieu de la mer. Elle dit : \q « Je suis comme une femme qui n’a pas d’enfants. Je n’ai jamais été en travail ni accouché. Je n’ai jamais élevé de garçons jusqu’à ce qu’ils soient des hommes, ni de filles jusqu’à ce qu’elles soient des femmes. »

sw.L: Ona aibu, Sidoni, kwa maana bahari imesema, \q ngome ya bahari, ikisema, \q "Sijaona utungu wala sijazaa, wala sijalea vijana wa kiume, [wala] sijakuza wasichana."
sw.B: Inamisha kichwa kwa aibu, Sidoni, \q kwa sababu bahari, ngome ya bahari, inalia: \q "Sijawahi kuwa na utungu wala kuzaa watoto; sijalea vijana wa kiume wala kukuza wasichana."
sw.R: Sidoni, ona aibu! \q Bahari imesema, ile ngome yenye nguvu iliyo baharini. Inasema, \q "Mimi ni kama mwanamke asiye na watoto. Sijawahi kuwa na utungu wala kuzaa. Sijawahi kulea wavulana wakawa vijana, wala wasichana wakawa wanawake."

decisions.choice: the sea, the stronghold of the sea: the sea speaks, and Tyre, its island fortress, speaks with it
alternatives: the sea, that is, Tyre the fortress of the sea
decisions.reason: The second phrase may name the sea again or name Tyre, the fortress set in the sea. Either way the voice is that of the sea and the city in it.

decisions.choice: I have not given birth: like a woman who has lost all her children
decisions.reason: The sea, which had been like a mother to the coastal cities, speaks as if she had never had children at all: her young people are gone. Sidon is shamed because the mother of her trade is left childless.

decisions.choice: I am like a woman who has no children
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture behind the sea's words.

records.literal_gloss: When [the] report [comes] to Egypt, they will be in anguish like [at] the report of Tyre.

en.L: When the report [comes] to Egypt, \q they will writhe at the report of Tyre.
en.B: When the news reaches Egypt, \q they will shake with pain at what they hear of Tyre.
en.R: When the people of Egypt hear the news about Tyre, \q they will tremble with grief.

es.L: Cuando la noticia [llegue] a Egipto, \q se retorcerán de dolor por la noticia de Tiro.
es.B: Cuando la noticia llegue a Egipto, \q se estremecerán de dolor por lo que oigan de Tiro.
es.R: Cuando la gente de Egipto oiga la noticia sobre Tiro, \q temblará de dolor.

fr.L: Quand la nouvelle [parviendra] à l’Égypte, \q ils se tordront de douleur à la nouvelle de Tyr.
fr.B: Quand la nouvelle arrivera en Égypte, \q ils trembleront de douleur en apprenant ce qui est arrivé à Tyr.
fr.R: Quand les gens d’Égypte apprendront la nouvelle au sujet de Tyr, \q ils trembleront de tristesse.

sw.L: Habari zitakapofika Misri, \q watagaagaa kwa ajili ya habari za Tiro.
sw.B: Habari zitakapoifikia Misri, \q watatetemeka kwa uchungu kwa yale watakayosikia kuhusu Tiro.
sw.R: Watu wa Misri watakaposikia habari za Tiro, \q watatetemeka kwa huzuni.

decisions.choice: when the report comes to Egypt, they will writhe at the report of Tyre
alternatives: as at the report about Egypt, so they will writhe at the report about Tyre
decisions.reason: The first word can mean "when" or "as". Read as "as", the line compares the two: as at the news about Egypt, so they will writhe at the news about Tyre. The reading "when" fits verse 3, where Egypt's grain trade depends on Tyre.

decisions.choice: be in anguish: writhe, as a woman in labor
decisions.reason: The verb describes twisting in pain, often of childbirth, and echoes the labor of verse 4.

records.literal_gloss: Pass over to Tarshish; wail, inhabitants of [the] coastland.

en.L: Cross over to Tarshish; \q wail, inhabitants of the coastland!
en.B: Sail away to Tarshish! \q Wail, you who live on the coast!
en.R: Escape by ship to Tarshish, far to the west! \q Cry out in grief, you people who live on the coast!

es.L: {{plural_you:Pasen|Pasad}} a Tarsis; \q ¡{{plural_you:giman|gemid}}, habitantes de la costa!
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Naveguen|Navegad}} hasta Tarsis! \q ¡{{plural_you:Giman, ustedes que viven|Gemid, vosotros que vivís}} en la costa!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Huyan|Huid}} en barco a Tarsis, lejos hacia el occidente! \q ¡{{plural_you:Lloren de dolor, ustedes que viven|Llorad de dolor, vosotros que vivís}} en la costa!

fr.L: Passez à Tarsis ; \q lamentez-vous, habitants de la côte !
fr.B: Embarquez pour Tarsis ! \q Lamentez-vous, vous qui habitez la côte !
fr.R: Fuyez en bateau jusqu’à Tarsis, loin vers l’ouest ! \q Criez de douleur, vous qui habitez sur la côte !

sw.L: Vukeni mpaka Tarshishi; \q ombolezeni, enyi wakaaji wa pwani!
sw.B: Safirini kwenda Tarshishi! \q Ombolezeni, enyi mnaoishi pwani!
sw.R: Kimbieni kwa meli mpaka Tarshishi, mbali kule magharibi! \q Lieni kwa huzuni, enyi watu mnaoishi pwani!

decisions.choice: cross over to Tarshish: flee by sea to the far west
decisions.reason: Tarshish was the most distant western port the Phoenicians sailed to (Jonah 1:3). The people of the coast are told to flee there as refugees.

decisions.choice: Escape by ship ... far to the west
decisions.reason: Readable says why they cross the sea and where Tarshish lay.

source.text: הֲזֹ֥את לָכֶ֖ם עַלִּיזָ֑ה מִֽימֵי־קֶ֤דֶם קַדְמָתָהּ֙ יֹבִל֣וּהָ רַגְלֶ֔יהָ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לָגֽוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] this to you [the] exultant [one], from days of antiquity [is] her beginning? Have carried her her feet from afar to sojourn.

en.L: Is this your exultant [city], \q whose beginning [is] from days of old? Her feet carried her far away to sojourn.
en.B: Is this your rejoicing city, \q whose story began in ancient days? Her own feet took her far away to make her home among strangers.
en.R: Is this really your happy, noisy city? \q Tyre was founded long, long ago. Her own feet took her far away to live as a stranger.

es.L: ¿Es esta {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} [ciudad] alborozada, \q cuyo origen [es] de los días antiguos? Sus pies la llevaron lejos a morar como extranjera.
es.B: ¿Es esta {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} ciudad llena de júbilo, \q cuya historia comenzó en tiempos antiguos? Sus propios pies la llevaron lejos a vivir entre extraños.
es.R: ¿Es esta de verdad {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} ciudad alegre y ruidosa? \q Tiro fue fundada hace muchísimo tiempo. Sus propios pies la llevaron lejos a vivir como extranjera.

fr.L: Est-ce là votre [cité] joyeuse, \q dont l’origine [remonte] aux jours d’autrefois ? Ses pieds la portaient au loin pour séjourner.
fr.B: Est-ce là votre ville en fête, \q dont l’histoire a commencé aux temps anciens ? Ses propres pieds l’ont menée au loin pour s’établir parmi des étrangers.
fr.R: Est-ce vraiment votre ville joyeuse et bruyante ? \q Tyr a été fondée il y a très, très longtemps. Ses propres pieds l’ont emmenée loin pour vivre comme une étrangère.

sw.L: Je, huu ndio [mji] wenu wa shangwe, \q ambao mwanzo wake [ni] tangu siku za kale? Miguu yake ilimchukua mbali kukaa ugenini.
sw.B: Je, huu ndio mji wenu wa furaha, \q ambao historia yake ilianza siku za kale? Miguu yake mwenyewe ilimpeleka mbali akakae kati ya wageni.
sw.R: Je, kweli huu ndio mji wenu wa furaha na kelele? \q Tiro ulianzishwa zamani sana. Miguu yake yenyewe ilimpeleka mbali akaishi kama mgeni.

decisions.choice: exultant: full of noisy joy and pride
decisions.reason: The word describes loud celebration, and in 22:2 and 32:13 a city given to revelry. The question mocks Tyre's old confidence.

decisions.choice: her feet carried her far away to sojourn: she went far off to live as a foreigner
alternatives: her people will be carried off to live in exile
decisions.reason: The line may look back on Tyre's traders who settled in colonies across the sea, or forward to her people driven into exile in foreign lands. The words allow both.

decisions.choice: Tyre was founded
decisions.reason: Readable names Tyre and says "founded" for "her beginning".

source.text: מִ֚י יָעַ֣ץ זֹ֔את עַל־צֹ֖ר הַמַּֽעֲטִירָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר סֹחֲרֶ֨יה֙ שָׂרִ֔ים כִּנְעָנֶ֖יהָ נִכְבַּדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose traders [were] princes, her merchants [were] [the] honored of [the] earth?

en.L: Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, \q whose traders [were] princes, \q her merchants the honored of the earth?
en.B: Who made this plan against Tyre, which once handed out crowns? \q Her traders ranked as princes; \q her merchants were honored across the earth.
en.R: Who planned this disaster for Tyre? Tyre was the city that gave out crowns. \q Her traders lived like princes. \q People all over the world honored her merchants.

es.L: ¿Quién planeó esto contra Tiro, la que otorgaba coronas, \q cuyos comerciantes [eran] príncipes, \q sus mercaderes, los honrados de la tierra?
es.B: ¿Quién trazó este plan contra Tiro, la que antes repartía coronas? \q Sus comerciantes eran como príncipes; \q sus mercaderes eran honrados en toda la tierra.
es.R: ¿Quién planeó este desastre contra Tiro? Tiro era la ciudad que repartía coronas. \q Sus comerciantes vivían como príncipes. \q La gente de todo el mundo honraba a sus mercaderes.

fr.L: Qui a décidé cela contre Tyr, la distributrice de couronnes, \q dont les marchands [étaient] des princes, \q ses trafiquants, les honorés de la terre ?
fr.B: Qui a formé ce projet contre Tyr, elle qui distribuait des couronnes ? \q Ses marchands avaient rang de princes ; \q ses trafiquants étaient honorés par toute la terre.
fr.R: Qui a décidé ce malheur pour Tyr ? Tyr était la ville qui donnait des couronnes. \q Ses marchands vivaient comme des princes. \q Partout dans le monde, on honorait ses commerçants.

sw.L: Ni nani aliyepanga jambo hili juu ya Tiro, mgawaji wa taji, \q ambaye wafanyabiashara wake [walikuwa] wakuu, \q wachuuzi wake waheshimiwa wa dunia?
sw.B: Ni nani aliyefanya mpango huu juu ya Tiro, uliokuwa ukigawa taji? \q Wafanyabiashara wake walihesabiwa kuwa wakuu; \q wachuuzi wake waliheshimiwa duniani kote.
sw.R: Ni nani aliyepanga maafa haya kwa ajili ya Tiro? Tiro ulikuwa mji uliotoa taji kwa wafalme. \q Wafanyabiashara wake waliishi kama wakuu. \q Watu duniani kote waliwaheshimu wachuuzi wake.

decisions.choice: the bestower of crowns: the city that set up kings
decisions.reason: Tyre made rulers in the colonies it founded. The form could also mean "the crowned city", the city wearing a crown.

decisions.choice: merchants: literally "her Canaanites"
decisions.reason: Because the Phoenicians, the people of Canaan's coast, were the great traders, "Canaanite" came to mean a merchant (Zephaniah 1:11; Proverbs 31:24).

decisions.choice: who planned this: a question answered in verse 9
decisions.reason: The question prepares for the answer that follows: the plan is God's.

source.text: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת יְעָצָ֑הּ לְחַלֵּל֙ גְּא֣וֹן כָּל־צְבִ֔י לְהָקֵ֖ל כָּל־נִכְבַּדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh of hosts planned it, to profane [the] pride of all splendor, to treat with contempt all [the] honored of [the] earth.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts planned it, \q to defile the pride of all splendor, \q to treat as light all the honored of the earth.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies planned it, \q to stain the pride that every splendor brings \q and to bring low all the earth's honored ones.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies planned it. \q He planned to take away the pride that people felt in their beauty and wealth. \q He planned to bring shame on all the famous people of the earth.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos lo planeó, \q para profanar el orgullo de toda hermosura, \q para rebajar a todos los honrados de la tierra.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos lo planeó, \q para manchar el orgullo que da todo esplendor \q y humillar a todos los honrados de la tierra.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos lo planeó. \q Planeó quitarle a la gente el orgullo que sentía por su belleza y su riqueza. \q Planeó avergonzar a todos los famosos de la tierra.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées l’a décidé, \q pour profaner l’orgueil de toute splendeur, \q pour rendre légers tous les honorés de la terre.
fr.B: C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées qui l’a décidé, \q pour flétrir l’orgueil que donne toute splendeur \q et pour abaisser tous les grands de la terre.
fr.R: C’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées qui l’a décidé. \q Il a voulu enlever aux gens l’orgueil qu’ils tiraient de leur beauté et de leur richesse. \q Il a voulu couvrir de honte toutes les personnes célèbres de la terre.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amelipanga, \q kuunajisi kiburi cha fahari yote, \q kuwadharau waheshimiwa wote wa dunia.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amelipanga, \q ili kuchafua kiburi kinacholetwa na kila fahari, \q na kuwashusha waheshimiwa wote wa dunia.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi amelipanga. \q Alipanga kuondoa kiburi ambacho watu walikuwa nacho kwa sababu ya uzuri na utajiri wao. \q Alipanga kuwaaibisha watu wote mashuhuri wa dunia.

decisions.choice: to defile: to make common what was held high
decisions.reason: The verb means to profane or treat as common. God strips away the honor in which Tyre's glory was held.

decisions.choice: to treat as light the honored: a play on heavy and light
decisions.reason: "Honored" comes from the root "heavy" and "treat with contempt" from the root "light": the weighty people of the earth will count for nothing. The same pair answers the question of verse 8 (compare 2:12-17).

decisions.choice: beauty and wealth
decisions.reason: Readable says what Tyre's splendor was.

source.text: עִבְרִ֥י אַרְצֵ֖ךְ כַּיְאֹ֑ר בַּת־תַּרְשִׁ֕ישׁ אֵ֖ין מֵ֥זַח עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: Pass over your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish; there is not a restraint any longer.

en.L: Pass through your land like the Nile, \q daughter of Tarshish; [there is] no longer a restraint.
en.B: Spread over your land as the Nile spreads, \q Daughter Tarshish; nothing holds you in any longer.
en.R: People of Tarshish, spread out over your land, as the Nile River floods over its banks. \q Nothing holds you back anymore.

es.L: Recorre tu tierra como el Nilo, \q hija de Tarsis; ya no [hay] cinturón que te sujete.
es.B: Extiéndete por tu tierra como se extiende el Nilo, \q hija de Tarsis; ya nada te retiene.
es.R: Pueblo de Tarsis, extiéndete por tu tierra, como el río Nilo cuando se desborda. \q Ya nada te detiene.

fr.L: Parcours ton pays comme le Nil, \q fille de Tarsis ; [il n’y a] plus de ceinture.
fr.B: Répands-toi sur ton pays comme le Nil se répand, \q fille de Tarsis ; plus rien ne te retient.
fr.R: Habitants de Tarsis, répandez-vous sur votre pays, comme le Nil déborde de ses rives. \q Plus rien ne vous retient.

sw.L: Pita katika nchi yako kama Naili, \q binti Tarshishi; hakuna tena kizuizi.
sw.B: Enea katika nchi yako kama Naili unavyoenea, \q Binti Tarshishi; hakuna tena kinachokuzuia.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Tarshishi, eneeni katika nchi yenu, kama mto Naili unavyofurika kingo zake. \q Hakuna tena kinachowazuia.

decisions.choice: pass through: the traditional Hebrew text
alternatives: work your land like the Nile
decisions.reason: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads "work your land", and the Septuagint has "work your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage". The traditional text is followed here: Tarshish may flow freely over its land like the Nile in flood.

decisions.choice: restraint: a belt or bond that holds something in
decisions.reason: The word is rare (Psalm 109:19 uses a related word for a belt). It most likely means that Tyre's hold over Tarshish is gone. A harbor or dock is another possible sense.

decisions.choice: People of Tarshish
decisions.reason: "Daughter Tarshish" pictures the people of the city as a young woman; Readable says "people of Tarshish".

decisions.choice: "binti Tarshishi" (L); "Binti Tarshishi" (B); "watu wa Tarshishi" (R)
decisions.reason: A city called "daughter" follows the pattern the terms note sets for Daughter Zion and Daughter Babylon (2 Kings 19:21; Psalm 137:8), here and in verse 12 for Sidon.

source.text: יָדוֹ֙ נָטָ֣ה עַל־הַיָּ֔ם הִרְגִּ֖יז מַמְלָכ֑וֹת יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה אֶל־כְּנַ֔עַן לַשְׁמִ֖ד מָעֻזְנֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: His hand he has stretched out over the sea; he has made tremble kingdoms. Yahweh has commanded concerning Canaan to destroy her strongholds.

en.L: His hand {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has stretched out over the sea; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made kingdoms tremble. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given command concerning Canaan, \q to destroy her strongholds.
en.B: He has reached out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand over the sea \q and set kingdoms trembling. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has issued orders against Canaan, \q that her fortresses be torn down.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand over the sea. \q He has made kingdoms shake with fear. \q He has given the order to destroy the fortresses of Canaan, the land of Tyre and Sidon.

es.L: Su mano ha extendido {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sobre el mar; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha hecho temblar los reinos. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dado orden acerca de Canaán, \q de destruir sus fortalezas.
es.B: Ha extendido {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano sobre el mar \q y ha hecho temblar los reinos. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dado órdenes contra Canaán, \q que sean derribadas sus fortalezas.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha levantado {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano sobre el mar. \q Ha hecho temblar de miedo a los reinos. \q Ha dado la orden de destruir las fortalezas de Canaán, la tierra de Tiro y Sidón.

fr.L: Sa main, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a étendue sur la mer ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait trembler des royaumes. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné un ordre au sujet de Canaan, \q pour détruire ses forteresses.
fr.B: Il a étendu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main sur la mer \q et fait trembler des royaumes. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné l’ordre contre Canaan \q d’abattre ses forteresses.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a levé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main au-dessus de la mer. \q Il a fait trembler de peur des royaumes. \q Il a donné l’ordre de détruire les forteresses de Canaan, le pays de Tyr et de Sidon.

sw.L: Mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ameunyosha juu ya bahari; \q amezitetemesha falme. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametoa amri kuhusu Kanaani, \q kuziangamiza ngome zake.
sw.B: Ameunyosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} juu ya bahari \q na kuzifanya falme zitetemeke. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametoa amri juu ya Kanaani, \q kwamba ngome zake zibomolewe.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameinua mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} juu ya bahari. \q Amezifanya falme zitetemeke kwa hofu. \q Ametoa amri ya kuziangamiza ngome za Kanaani, nchi ya Tiro na Sidoni.

decisions.choice: his hand stretched out over the sea: God's power over the sea
decisions.reason: The stretched-out hand is God's hand of judgment (5:25; 14:26-27). Over the sea, it recalls the crossing of the sea in Exodus 14:21.

decisions.choice: Canaan: the Phoenician coast
decisions.reason: Here Canaan means the coastland of Tyre and Sidon, the old name for the land of the Phoenicians (Genesis 10:15).

decisions.choice: the LORD as subject; the land of Tyre and Sidon
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD at the start and says which part of Canaan is meant.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֥יפִי ע֖וֹד לַעְל֑וֹז הַֽמְעֻשָּׁקָ֞ה בְּתוּלַ֣ת בַּת־צִיד֗וֹן כִּתִּים֙ ק֣וּמִי עֲבֹ֔רִי גַּם־שָׁ֖ם לֹא־יָנ֥וּחַֽ לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, not you will again exult, O oppressed one, virgin daughter of Sidon; [to] Kittim arise, pass over; also there not it will be rest to you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said: You will not again exult, \q oppressed one, virgin daughter of Sidon! [To] Kittim, arise, cross over; \q even there [there] will be no rest for you.
en.B: He said: You will celebrate no more, \q you ravaged virgin, Daughter Sidon. Get up, cross over to Kittim; \q even there no rest awaits you.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said this: People of Sidon, you will never celebrate again. \q You are like a young woman who has been crushed. Get up and escape by ship to Cyprus. \q But even there you will not find rest.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dijo: No volverás a alborozarte, \q oh oprimida, virgen hija de Sidón. ¡A Quitim, levántate, pasa! \q Ni aun allí habrá descanso para ti.
es.B: Y él dijo: Nunca más volverás a celebrar, \q virgen violentada, hija de Sidón. Levántate, pasa a Quitim; \q ni aun allí te espera descanso.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: Pueblo de Sidón, nunca volverás a celebrar. \q Eres como una joven que ha sido aplastada. Levántate y huye en barco a Chipre. \q Pero ni siquiera allí encontrarás descanso.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : Tu ne te réjouiras plus, \q opprimée, vierge, fille de Sidon ! Vers les Kittim, lève-toi, passe ; \q même là, [il n’y] aura pas de repos pour toi.
fr.B: Il a dit : Tu ne feras plus la fête, \q vierge violentée, fille de Sidon. Lève-toi, passe chez les Kittim ; \q même là, aucun repos ne t’attend.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit : Habitants de Sidon, vous ne ferez plus jamais la fête. \q Vous êtes comme une jeune femme qu’on a écrasée. Levez-vous, fuyez en bateau jusqu’à Chypre. \q Mais même là, vous ne trouverez pas de repos.

sw.L: Naye akasema: Hutashangilia tena, \q ewe uliyeonewa, binti bikira wa Sidoni! [Kwenda] Kitimu, inuka, vuka; \q hata huko hapatakuwa na raha kwako.
sw.B: Alisema: Hutasherehekea tena, \q ewe bikira uliyeharibiwa, Binti Sidoni. Inuka, vuka uende Kitimu; \q hata huko hakuna raha inayokungoja.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema hivi: Enyi watu wa Sidoni, hamtasherehekea tena kamwe. \q Mko kama msichana aliyepondwa. Inukeni mkimbie kwa meli mpaka Kipro. \q Lakini hata huko hamtapata raha.

decisions.choice: he said: the LORD of verse 11
decisions.reason: The speaker is not named; the nearest is the LORD, who gave the command against Canaan in verse 11.

decisions.choice: oppressed virgin: a city never taken, now crushed and violated
decisions.reason: The city is pictured as a young woman. "Virgin" marks her as never conquered; the verb means crushed or wronged by force (compare 47:1).

decisions.choice: Kittim: Cyprus
decisions.reason: Refugees from Sidon would flee to Cyprus, where the Phoenicians had colonies (verse 1). The written text has a longer spelling of the same name; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: People of Sidon ... like a young woman who has been crushed
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, speaks to the people, and states the picture as a comparison.

source.text: הֵ֣ן׀אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה אַשּׁ֖וּר יְסָדָ֣הּ לְצִיִּ֑ים הֵקִ֣ימוּ בַחוּנָ֗יו עֹרְרוּ֙ אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ שָׂמָ֖הּ לְמַפֵּלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, [the] land of [the] Chaldeans, this [is] the people [that] not was; Assyria assigned it to desert creatures. They raised up its siege towers, they laid bare its palaces, it made it into a ruin.

en.L: Look, the land of the Chaldeans! This [is] the people [that] is no more; \q Assyria assigned it to desert creatures. \q They raised up its siege towers; they stripped its palaces; \q [one] made it a ruin.
en.B: See the land of the Chaldeans, a people who no longer exist! \q Assyria gave it over to the beasts of the wilderness. \q Its siege towers went up, its palaces were torn bare, \q and it was left a heap of rubble.
en.R: Look at what happened to the land of Babylonia. Its people are gone. \q The Assyrians turned it into a place where only wild animals live. \q They built towers to attack the city. They tore down its palaces and left it in ruins.

es.L: He aquí la tierra de los caldeos: este [es] el pueblo [que] ya no existe; \q Asiria la destinó a las fieras del desierto. \q Levantaron sus torres de asedio; despojaron sus palacios; \q la convirtió en una ruina.
es.B: Mira la tierra de los caldeos, un pueblo que ya no existe. \q Asiria la entregó a las fieras del desierto. \q Se alzaron sus torres de asedio, sus palacios quedaron desnudos, \q y quedó hecha un montón de escombros.
es.R: Mira lo que le pasó a la tierra de Babilonia. Su pueblo ya no existe. \q Los asirios la convirtieron en un lugar donde solo viven animales salvajes. \q Construyeron torres para atacar la ciudad. Derribaron sus palacios y la dejaron en ruinas.

fr.L: Voici le pays des Chaldéens ! Ce peuple n’existe plus ; \q l’Assyrie l’a livré aux bêtes du désert. \q Ils ont dressé ses tours de siège ; ils ont mis à nu ses palais ; \q [on] l’a réduit en ruine.
fr.B: Regardez le pays des Chaldéens, un peuple qui n’existe plus ! \q L’Assyrie l’a abandonné aux bêtes sauvages du désert. \q Ses tours de siège se sont dressées, ses palais ont été dépouillés, \q et il n’est plus qu’un tas de décombres.
fr.R: Regardez ce qui est arrivé au pays de Babylone. Son peuple a disparu. \q Les Assyriens en ont fait un endroit où ne vivent plus que des bêtes sauvages. \q Ils ont construit des tours pour attaquer la ville. Ils ont démoli ses palais et l’ont laissée en ruine.

sw.L: Tazama, nchi ya Wakaldayo! Hawa [ndio] watu [ambao] hawako tena; \q Ashuru iliikabidhi kwa viumbe vya jangwani. \q Waliinua minara yake ya kuzingira; wakayavua majumba yake ya kifalme; \q akaifanya kuwa magofu.
sw.B: Tazameni nchi ya Wakaldayo, watu ambao hawapo tena! \q Ashuru iliikabidhi kwa wanyama wa nyikani. \q Minara yake ya kuzingira ilisimamishwa, majumba yake ya kifalme yakavuliwa kabisa, \q nayo ikaachwa kuwa rundo la kifusi.
sw.R: Tazameni yaliyoipata nchi ya Babeli. Watu wake wametoweka. \q Waashuru waliifanya kuwa mahali ambapo wanyama wa porini tu wanaishi. \q Walijenga minara ili kuushambulia mji. Walibomoa majumba yake ya kifalme na kuuacha magofu.

decisions.choice: this is the people that is no more; Assyria assigned it
decisions.reason: The words may also be read "this is the people; it was not Assyria", setting the Chaldeans against Assyria. Read as here, the verse points to Babylon's ruin at Assyria's hands (Sennacherib destroyed Babylon in 689 BC): if Babylon could fall, so can Tyre.

decisions.choice: desert creatures: wild animals of the dry places
decisions.reason: The word means those who live in the desert, animals or nomads; it is used for wild creatures in ruins in 13:21 and 34:14.

decisions.choice: siege towers: towers built against a city's walls
decisions.reason: The word is rare; it names the towers an army raised to attack a city. The written text and the scribes' reading differ only in a vowel letter.

decisions.choice: Babylonia
decisions.reason: Readable says "Babylonia" for "the land of the Chaldeans", the people who lived in southern Babylonia.

decisions.choice: los caldeos (L, B); Babilonia (R)
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans keep their name at L and B, as 2 Kings 25:4-5; Readable names Babylonia, as the English R.

decisions.choice: "Wakaldayo" (L, B); "nchi ya Babeli" (R)
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans are "Wakaldayo" as 2 Chronicles 36:17 and the terms note; Readable names the land, as the English "Babylonia".

decisions.choice: "les Chaldéens" (L, B), "Babylone" (R), for Isaiah 21-40
decisions.reason: As the terms note and 2 Kings 25; Readable gives the better known name, as the English Readable.

source.text: הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מָעֻזְּכֶֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Wail, ships of Tarshish, for has been devastated your stronghold.

en.L: Wail, ships of Tarshish, \q for your stronghold is devastated!
en.B: Wail, ships of Tarshish, \q for your fortress has been laid waste!
en.R: Cry out in grief, you sailors on the great trading ships! \q The strong city where you were safe has been destroyed.

es.L: {{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, naves de Tarsis, \q ¡porque {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fortaleza ha sido devastada!
es.B: {{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, naves de Tarsis, \q ¡porque {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fortaleza ha sido asolada!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Lloren de dolor, ustedes|Llorad de dolor, vosotros}}, marineros de los grandes barcos mercantes! \q La ciudad fuerte donde {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} seguros ha sido destruida.

fr.L: Lamentez-vous, navires de Tarsis, \q car votre forteresse est dévastée !
fr.B: Lamentez-vous, navires de Tarsis, \q car votre forteresse a été ravagée !
fr.R: Criez de douleur, vous, les marins des grands navires de commerce ! \q La ville forte où vous étiez en sécurité a été détruite.

sw.L: Ombolezeni, enyi merikebu za Tarshishi, \q kwa maana ngome yenu imeharibiwa!
sw.B: Ombolezeni, enyi merikebu za Tarshishi, \q kwa maana ngome yenu imeangamizwa!
sw.R: Lieni kwa huzuni, enyi mabaharia wa meli kubwa za biashara! \q Mji wenye nguvu ambamo mlikuwa salama umeangamizwa.

decisions.choice: wail, ships of Tarshish: the poem ends as it began
decisions.reason: The cry repeats verse 1 and closes the poem; the stronghold is Tyre, the home port of the ships.

decisions.choice: great trading ships
decisions.reason: Readable says what ships of Tarshish were: large ships built for long trading voyages (2:16). Readable speaks to the sailors on them.

decisions.choice: the strong city where you were safe
decisions.reason: Readable says what the ships' stronghold was.

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְנִשְׁכַּ֤חַת צֹר֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה כִּימֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶחָ֑ד מִקֵּ֞ץ שִׁבְעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לְצֹ֔ר כְּשִׁירַ֖ת הַזּוֹנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be in the day the that, and [will be] forgotten Tyre seventy years like [the] days of a king one; from [the] end of seventy years it will be to Tyre like the song of the prostitute:

en.L: And it will be in that day that Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will be for Tyre like the song of the prostitute:
en.B: On that day Tyre will drop out of memory for seventy years, as long as one king's lifetime. At the close of those seventy years, Tyre's story will be like the prostitute's song:
en.R: At that time people will forget about Tyre for seventy years. That is about as long as a king lives. After the seventy years, Tyre will be like the woman in this song about a prostitute:

es.L: Y sucederá en aquel día que Tiro será olvidada setenta años, como los días de un rey. Al cabo de setenta años le sucederá a Tiro como en la canción de la prostituta:
es.B: Aquel día Tiro caerá en el olvido durante setenta años, lo que dura la vida de un rey. Al terminar esos setenta años, a Tiro le pasará lo que dice la canción de la prostituta:
es.R: En ese tiempo la gente se olvidará de Tiro durante setenta años. Eso es más o menos lo que vive un rey. Después de los setenta años, Tiro será como la mujer de esta canción sobre una prostituta:

fr.L: Et il arrivera en ce jour-là que Tyr sera oubliée soixante-dix ans, comme les jours d’un seul roi. Au bout de soixante-dix ans, il en sera pour Tyr comme [dans] la chanson de la prostituée :
fr.B: Ce jour-là, Tyr tombera dans l’oubli pendant soixante-dix ans, la durée de la vie d’un roi. Au terme de ces soixante-dix ans, il arrivera à Tyr ce que dit la chanson de la prostituée :
fr.R: En ce temps-là, on oubliera Tyr pendant soixante-dix ans. C’est à peu près le temps que vit un roi. Après ces soixante-dix ans, Tyr sera comme la femme de cette chanson sur une prostituée :

sw.L: Na itakuwa katika siku ile, Tiro utasahauliwa miaka sabini, kama siku za mfalme mmoja. Mwishoni mwa miaka sabini itakuwa kwa Tiro kama wimbo wa kahaba:
sw.B: Siku hiyo Tiro utasahauliwa kwa miaka sabini, muda wa maisha ya mfalme mmoja. Mwishoni mwa miaka hiyo sabini, habari ya Tiro itakuwa kama wimbo wa kahaba:
sw.R: Wakati huo watu watausahau Tiro kwa miaka sabini. Huo ni karibu muda ambao mfalme mmoja anaishi. Baada ya miaka hiyo sabini, Tiro utakuwa kama mwanamke katika wimbo huu kuhusu kahaba:

decisions.choice: seventy years: a full lifetime of judgment
decisions.reason: Seventy years is a full human life (Psalm 90:10) and the length Jeremiah gives for the nations' service to Babylon (Jeremiah 25:11-12; 29:10).

decisions.choice: like the days of one king: the length of one reign or lifetime
alternatives: like the reign of one dynasty
decisions.reason: The phrase means a long but limited span: one king's reign, or a lifetime. It may also mean an unchanging time, as under a single king.

decisions.choice: the song of the prostitute: a popular song, quoted in verse 16
decisions.reason: The song mocks an aging prostitute who must sing in the streets to be noticed again. Trade for profit is pictured as prostitution, as with Nineveh in Nahum 3:4.

source.text: קְחִ֥י כִנּ֛וֹר סֹ֥בִּי עִ֖יר זוֹנָ֣ה נִשְׁכָּחָ֑ה הֵיטִ֤יבִי נַגֵּן֙ הַרְבִּי־שִׁ֔יר לְמַ֖עַן תִּזָּכֵֽרִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Take a harp, go around [the] city, O prostitute forgotten; do well playing, multiply song, so that you may be remembered.

en.L: "Take a harp, go around the city, forgotten prostitute! \q Play well, sing many songs, \q so that you may be remembered."
en.B: "Pick up a harp and walk through the city, you prostitute whom everyone forgot! \q Play sweetly, sing song after song, \q so that someone will remember you."
en.R: "You prostitute whom everyone has forgotten, take your harp and walk around the city. \q Play your music well. Sing many songs so that people will remember you."

es.L: «Toma un arpa, recorre la ciudad, prostituta olvidada; \q toca bien, multiplica las canciones, \q para que seas recordada».
es.B: «Toma un arpa y recorre la ciudad, prostituta a quien todos olvidaron; \q toca con dulzura, canta canción tras canción, \q para que alguien se acuerde de ti».
es.R: «Prostituta a quien todos han olvidado, toma tu arpa y recorre la ciudad. \q Toca bien tu música. Canta muchas canciones para que la gente se acuerde de ti».

fr.L: « Prends une harpe, fais le tour de la ville, prostituée oubliée ! \q Joue bien, multiplie les chansons, \q afin qu’on se souvienne de toi. »
fr.B: « Prends une harpe et parcours la ville, prostituée que tout le monde a oubliée ! \q Joue avec douceur, chante chanson sur chanson, \q pour qu’on se souvienne de toi. »
fr.R: « Prostituée que tout le monde a oubliée, prends ta harpe et fais le tour de la ville. \q Joue bien de ta musique. Chante beaucoup de chansons pour qu’on se souvienne de toi. »

sw.L: "Chukua kinubi, zunguka mjini, ewe kahaba uliyesahauliwa! \q Piga vizuri, imba nyimbo nyingi, \q ili ukumbukwe."
sw.B: "Shika kinubi utembee mjini, ewe kahaba ambaye kila mtu amekusahau! \q Piga kwa utamu, imba wimbo baada ya wimbo, \q ili mtu akukumbuke."
sw.R: "Ewe kahaba ambaye kila mtu amekusahau, chukua kinubi chako utembee mjini. \q Piga muziki wako vizuri. Imba nyimbo nyingi ili watu wakukumbuke."

decisions.choice: take a harp, go around: the words of the song
decisions.reason: The verse is the song named in verse 15. It speaks to the forgotten prostitute, a picture of Tyre after seventy years.

decisions.choice: harp: a stringed instrument held in the hands
decisions.reason: The word is the lyre played at feasts and in worship (5:12; Genesis 4:21).

source.text: וְהָיָ֞ה מִקֵּ֣ץ׀שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה יִפְקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־צֹ֔ר וְשָׁבָ֖ה לְאֶתְנַנָּ֑ה וְזָֽנְתָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be from [the] end of seventy years, will visit Yahweh Tyre, and she will return to her hire and she will prostitute herself with all [the] kingdoms of the earth on [the] face of the ground.

en.L: And it will be at the end of seventy years [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will visit Tyre, and she will return to her wages and will play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the earth on the face of the ground.
en.B: At the end of the seventy years {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will turn {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} attention to Tyre. She will go back to earning her fee, selling herself to every kingdom of the world across the face of the earth.
en.R: After seventy years, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come to help Tyre again. Then she will go back to trading for profit, like a prostitute who sells herself for pay. She will do business with all the kingdoms of the world.

es.L: Y sucederá al cabo de setenta años [que] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} visitará a Tiro, y ella volverá a su paga y se prostituirá con todos los reinos de la tierra sobre la faz del suelo.
es.B: Al cabo de los setenta años {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} volverá {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} atención a Tiro. Ella volverá a ganar su paga, vendiéndose a todos los reinos del mundo sobre la faz de la tierra.
es.R: Después de setenta años, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vendrá otra vez a ayudar a Tiro. Entonces ella volverá a comerciar para ganar dinero, como una prostituta que se vende por dinero. Hará negocios con todos los reinos del mundo.

fr.L: Et il arrivera au bout de soixante-dix ans [que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} visitera Tyr, et elle retournera à son salaire et se prostituera avec tous les royaumes de la terre sur la face du sol.
fr.B: Au bout des soixante-dix ans, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} se tournera vers Tyr. Elle reprendra son métier pour gagner son salaire, et elle se vendra à tous les royaumes du monde sur la face de la terre.
fr.R: Après soixante-dix ans, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} viendra de nouveau aider Tyr. Alors elle recommencera à faire du commerce pour gagner de l’argent, comme une prostituée qui se vend pour un salaire. Elle fera des affaires avec tous les royaumes du monde.

sw.L: Na itakuwa mwishoni mwa miaka sabini, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atamjilia Tiro, naye atarudia ujira wake, na kufanya ukahaba na falme zote za dunia juu ya uso wa nchi.
sw.B: Mwishoni mwa miaka hiyo sabini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atauelekezea Tiro uangalifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Naye atarudia kupata ujira wake, akijiuza kwa kila ufalme wa dunia katika uso wote wa nchi.
sw.R: Baada ya miaka sabini, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuja kuusaidia Tiro tena. Kisha Tiro utarudia biashara ya kutafuta faida, kama kahaba anayejiuza kwa malipo. Utafanya biashara na falme zote za dunia.

decisions.choice: visit: attend to, here to restore
decisions.reason: The verb means to give attention to someone, for judgment or for help. After the seventy years God attends to Tyre and allows her to rise again (compare Jeremiah 29:10).

decisions.choice: her wages, play the prostitute: trade for profit with the nations
decisions.reason: The picture of verse 15 continues. Tyre's trade with every kingdom is like a prostitute's dealings with her clients: done for pay, with no loyalty (compare Nahum 3:4; Ezekiel 27).

decisions.choice: trading for profit, like a prostitute
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means and keeps it as a comparison.

decisions.choice: turn his attention to / come to help
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "visit"; Balanced and Readable say what the visit means here.

source.text: וְהָיָ֨ה סַחְרָ֜הּ וְאֶתְנַנָּ֗הּ קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א יֵֽאָצֵ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יֵֽחָסֵ֑ן כִּ֣י לַיֹּשְׁבִ֞ים לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה סַחְרָ֔הּ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל לְשָׂבְעָ֖ה וְלִמְכַסֶּ֥ה עָתִֽיק׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And will be her trading profit and her hire a holy thing to Yahweh; not it will be stored up and not it will be hoarded, for to those dwelling before Yahweh will belong her trading profit, for eating to satiety and for covering magnificent.

en.L: And her profit and her wages will be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it will not be stored up and will not be hoarded, for her profit will belong to those who dwell before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for eating to the full and for splendid covering.
en.B: Yet what she gains and what she is paid will be holy, belonging to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. No one will lock it away or pile it up. Her earnings will go to those who live in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to give them all the food they want and splendid clothing.
en.R: But the money Tyre earns will be given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It will be holy. No one will save it up or keep it for themselves. It will go to the people who live in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will have plenty to eat and fine clothes to wear.

es.L: Y su ganancia y su paga serán cosa consagrada {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}; no será almacenada ni será atesorada, porque su ganancia será para los que habitan delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, para comer hasta saciarse y para vestidura espléndida.
es.B: Pero lo que gane y lo que le paguen será sagrado, y pertenecerá {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Nadie lo guardará bajo llave ni lo amontonará. Sus ganancias irán a los que viven en la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, para que tengan toda la comida que quieran y ropa espléndida.
es.R: Pero el dinero que gane Tiro será entregado {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Será sagrado. Nadie lo ahorrará ni se lo quedará para sí. Será para la gente que vive en la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Tendrán comida en abundancia y ropa fina para vestir.

fr.L: Et son gain et son salaire seront consacrés {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ; ils ne seront pas mis en réserve et ne seront pas amassés, car son gain sera pour ceux qui habitent devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, pour manger à satiété et pour un vêtement magnifique.
fr.B: Mais ce qu’elle gagnera et ce qu’on lui paiera sera sacré, consacré {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Personne ne le mettra sous clé ni ne l’amassera. Ses gains iront à ceux qui vivent en présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, pour leur donner toute la nourriture qu’ils voudront et de magnifiques vêtements.
fr.R: Mais l’argent que Tyr gagnera sera donné {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Il sera sacré. Personne ne le mettra de côté ni ne le gardera pour soi. Il ira aux gens qui vivent en présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Ils auront à manger en abondance et de beaux vêtements à porter.

sw.L: Na faida yake na ujira wake vitakuwa vitakatifu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; havitawekwa akiba wala havitalimbikizwa, kwa maana faida yake itakuwa ya wale wanaokaa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa ajili ya kula na kushiba na kwa ajili ya mavazi ya fahari.
sw.B: Lakini anachokipata na anacholipwa kitakuwa kitakatifu, mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hakuna atakayekifungia wala kukilimbikiza. Mapato yake yatawaendea wale wanaoishi mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wapate chakula chote wanachotaka na mavazi ya fahari.
sw.R: Lakini fedha ambazo Tiro unapata zitatolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Zitakuwa takatifu. Hakuna mtu atakayeziweka akiba au kujiwekea mwenyewe. Zitawaendea watu wanaoishi mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Watakuwa na chakula tele na mavazi mazuri ya kuvaa.

decisions.choice: holy to the LORD: set apart for God
decisions.reason: Tyre's earnings, once the wages of her trade, will be dedicated to God. The nations' wealth comes to God's people again in 60:5-11 and 61:6.

decisions.choice: those who dwell before the LORD: those who serve in God's presence
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the priests and worshipers at the temple, or more widely God's people who live before him.

decisions.choice: splendid covering: fine clothing
decisions.reason: The covering is clothing; the rare adjective means choice or magnificent.
